external_entities.name: shopper
external_entities.description: A shopper who browses the storefront and places orders.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders

external_entities.name: card processor
external_entities.description: A third-party card processor that settles payments and sends a webhook to the storefront API.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

processes.name: storefront API
processes.description: A Node service running on Cloud Run that shoppers use to browse and place orders and that receives payment webhooks.
processes.source_excerpt: the storefront API, a Node service running on Cloud Run
processes.technology: Node service running on Cloud Run

processes.name: order service
processes.description: A Python worker in the core network that accepts orders from the storefront API, reads and writes the orders database, and writes completed-order receipts.
processes.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

data_stores.name: orders-db
data_stores.description: A PostgreSQL database containing orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database (orders-db)

data_stores.name: receipt archive
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket containing receipts for completed orders.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive

data_flows.name: place order
data_flows.description: A shopper browses the storefront and places an order through the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API

data_flows.name: submit order
data_flows.description: The storefront API submits a shopper order to the order service over gRPC.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC

data_flows.name: read and write
data_flows.description: The order service reads and writes orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four in orders-db.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the order service reads and writes with a single application account that has full read/write
data_flows.authentication: single application account; password from an environment variable on the worker

data_flows.name: write receipt
data_flows.description: The order service writes a receipt for each completed order to the receipt archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive.
data_flows.authentication: the order service's own service account
data_flows.data_description: Receipt recording which order was written and that the order service wrote it

data_flows.name: settlement webhook
data_flows.description: The card processor sends a webhook to the storefront API after settling a payment to report that the order is paid.
data_flows.source_excerpt: After they settle a payment they POST a webhook back to the storefront API to tell us the order is paid.
data_flows.notes: The source states: "I would have to check how that callback is authenticated."

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The internet-facing zone containing the storefront API and shoppers.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: It is the only thing we expose to the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: core network
trust_boundaries.description: The internal core network containing the order service and order data stores.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

trust_boundaries.name: card processor
trust_boundaries.description: The third-party zone in which the card processor operates.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

assumptions.assumption: The storefront API presents a web interface.
assumptions.basis: It is described as a storefront API that receives an HTTP POST webhook; HTTP application APIs are web interfaces.

assumptions.assumption: The order service presents a non-web interface.
assumptions.basis: The service is reached over gRPC, which is an RPC contract rather than a web application interface.
It contains shopper addresses and card-last-four, which are personal and payment data.
